evidenceAudit.scope: Adults with end-stage COPD and refractory breathlessness: oxygen criteria, home NIV, opioid and other drug options, palliative and hospice access. Verified against the Saudi Thoracic Society COPD guideline 2025, NICE NG115 (palliative care) and MOH Protocol-010.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: Benzodiazepine and other agent doses — local protocol

pathophysiology.summary: End-stage COPD causes severe breathlessness, frequent exacerbations and chronic respiratory failure despite maximal inhaled therapy. Supportive care targets breathlessness, anxiety and planning for deterioration.
keyMechanisms: Hyperinflation and gas-exchange failure cause breathlessness and hypoxaemia; some develop chronic hypercapnia.
Chronic hypoxaemia → pulmonary hypertension and cor pulmonale (STS).
Opioids reduce the sensation of breathlessness (NICE NG115).

symptoms: Breathlessness at rest or minimal exertion, fatigue, weight loss, anxiety, frequent admissions.
physicalSigns: Cyanosis, oedema (cor pulmonale), cachexia, accessory muscle use.
redFlags: Persistent hypercapnia 2 weeks after an exacerbation — consider home NIV (STS)

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Acute change — treat per AECOPD topic if consistent with goals.

ruleIn.testName: Resting SpO2 and arterial blood gas (stable)
ruleIn.expectedFinding: PaO2 below 55 mmHg (7.3 kPa), or 55–60 with cor pulmonale/oedema/haematocrit 55%+; persistent PaCO2 rise.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: LTOT if criteria met; NIV if hypercapnic 2 weeks after exacerbation (STS).

ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Consider opioids and other options (NICE NG115).

clinicalManagement.title: Optimise
actions: Maximal inhaled therapy, pulmonary rehabilitation where possible, smoking cessation (see COPD topic).

clinicalManagement.title: Oxygen and ventilation
actions: LTOT only if STS criteria met; at least 18 h/day, 1–2.5 L/min, target SaO2 88–94% (STS).
Home NIV if persistently hypercapnic 2 weeks after exacerbation (STS).

clinicalManagement.title: Palliate breathlessness
actions: Use opioids for refractory breathlessness (NICE NG115); morphine starting doses per MOH Protocol-010.
Consider benzodiazepines, tricyclic antidepressants or major tranquillisers when appropriate (NICE NG115).
Access to multidisciplinary palliative care and hospice (NICE NG115).

clinicalManagement.title: Advance care planning
actions: Discuss ceilings of care (NIV, intubation), preferred place of care; anticipatory medicines (NICE NG31).

learningObjectives: Relieve symptoms and plan care for people with end-stage COPD.

pitfalls: Oxygen for breathlessness without hypoxaemia criteria.
Avoiding opioids from fear of respiratory depression.

patientEducation: Action plan for exacerbations and goals of care.
lifestyleAndDiet: Stop smoking/shisha; pulmonary rehabilitation as able.
dischargeCriteria: Symptoms controlled in the preferred place of care; anticipatory plan documented.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Respiratory and palliative review after each admission and when symptoms change; LTOT review at 3 months and 1 year (STS).

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: PaO2 below 55 mmHg, or 55–60 with cor pulmonale/oedema/haematocrit 55% or more (STS)

regimens.dose: 5–10 mg PO (usual 5–15 mg), or 2.5–5 mg IV
regimens.frequency: Every 4 h as needed (IV every 3–4 h)
adjustments: Start low in frailty and renal impairment — seek specialist advice (NICE CG140)
regimens.sourceTitle: Protocols for Palliative Care Patients — End of Life Care (MOH Protocol-010)
regimens.sourceEdition: Saudi MOH, General Administration of Pharmaceutical Care, p. 9 (morphine initial doses)
contraindications: Acute or severe asthma without monitoring/resuscitation
Known or suspected GI obstruction including paralytic ileus

medicationPlan.note: Morphine starting doses from MOH Protocol-010 (pain indication); NICE NG115 recommends opioids for refractory breathlessness without a dose. Check SFDA registration and controlled-drug rules.
